declarations.docstring: The tensor product of two finite-dimensional complex representations of a finite group is isomorphic to a decomposition indexed by pairwise nonisomorphic simple representations that exhaust all simple objects.

For a complete finite family of pairwise nonisomorphic simple representations, the dimension of morphisms into a tensor product is the sum of tensor-product multiplicities weighted by the corresponding morphism-space dimensions.
A tensor product is isomorphic to the specified auxiliary decomposition whenever the indexing family is simple, pairwise nonisomorphic, and exhaustive among simple representations.
An auxiliary finite-dimensional representation associated with an indexed family and two representations.
A natural-number multiplicity attached to three finite-dimensional complex representations of a group.
The complex cast of the tensor-product multiplicity is the group average of the product of two characters with the inverse-argument character of the third representation.
